slides.texto_narrado: Here's the planting mistake almost nobody questions — they follow the date on the seed packet like it's gospel.
I did too. Right month, right depth, exactly what it said — and still lost half my tomato seedlings to a frost it never warned me about.
Turns out that packet date isn't written for your yard. It's written for an entire climate zone at once, which means it's really written for *no one's* yard.
The number that actually matters is your own average last frost date — and depending where you live, that can be *weeks* off from what the packet assumes.
